questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered an essential organic component for enriching the soil in a School Kitchen Garden?
A wheelbarrow used in a garden to transport heavy soil is an example of which type of simple machine?
In a school Biodiversity Register, observing and recording the migration pattern of local birds falls under which category?
Fill in the blank: A ______ is a simple machine consisting of a grooved wheel and a rope, often used to draw water from a well or lift heavy objects in Maker Skills projects.
What is the primary tool used to safely turn over and loosen the topsoil when preparing a new plot for a kitchen garden?

sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Answer (VSA) / Definitions

questions.question_text: Define what a 'pulley' is and give one practical example of its use in daily life or a school project. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A pulley is a simple machine featuring a wheel with a grooved rim and a rope. A practical example is using a pulley to hoist a school flag up a flagpole.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of adding 'mulch' (like dried leaves or grass) to the soil in a kitchen garden? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Adding mulch to a kitchen garden helps retain vital soil moisture, suppresses the growth of unwanted weeds, and gradually improves soil fertility as the organic matter decomposes.

questions.question_text: In the context of creating a Biodiversity Register, explain what the term 'Flora' means. [15-25 words]
questions.answer: The term 'Flora' refers exclusively to all the plant life occurring in a specific region or time, such as the trees and shrubs found in the school compound.

questions.question_text: Your group is tasked with setting up a small Kitchen Garden in the school yard to grow spinach and radishes. Outline the first three essential steps you must take to prepare the land before actually sowing the seeds. [35-45 words]
questions.answer: First, select a sunny spot and clear away all large stones and harmful weeds. Second, use a spade to dig, turn, and loosen the compacted topsoil thoroughly. Finally, mix in rich organic compost to ensure the soil has enough nutrients before planting the seeds.
